reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly, so the next check is whether each refund corresponds to a real order and is not larger than that order's amount. I'll list the orders.

Both refunds match real orders (130 and 133, both acme) and neither exceeds its order amount, so the refund work looks consistent with the ledger. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 28879 matches my own check: orders 130 and 133 total 43840, minus refunds 8178 and 6783 (14961), which leaves 28879. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 70733 matches the orders (131 and 134 total 70733) with no refunds against birch. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 16841 matches its orders 132 and 135 (10547 + 6294) with no refunds, so every customer checks out and Alpha's refunds are consistent with the ledger. I'll record the first payout, for acme at 28879.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance of 70733 matched my own check against orders 131 and 134 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 16841 matched my check against orders 132 and 135 with no refunds, so I'll record that as the last payout.
All three customers have been paid once, and each amount matched the net balance I checked against the orders and refunds. The task is complete, so I'm reporting the payouts.
